stories.headline: GDPx benchmark replaces GDP with real-world domain expertise for frontier models
stories.dek: SemiAnalysis partnered with specialized vendors to build agentic tasks in 11 high-value domains, revealing safety classifiers and meaningful performance gaps.
stories.summary:
SemiAnalysis released GDPx, a frontier model benchmark designed to replace the year-old GDPval by measuring capabilities where AI will have the highest ROI—not across the entire economy. The benchmark covers 11 domains: chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, legal, quant trading, recursive self-improvement, hardware design, materials science, alignment, and software engineering.

GDPval's core problem: it was built before agents became viable and treats tasks as isolated, well-scoped prompts with embedded context. A finance example asks models to write a 15-page PDF recommendation from a single reference document—work a human would perform through extensive research in a data room. GDPx inverts this. Finance tasks, built with Living Context, pull from real deal environments with ~4,000 anonymized files organized as a virtual data room. The model must navigate, retrieve context, and synthesize just as a human associate would.

To build domain-specific tasks rigorously, SemiAnalysis partnered with specialized RL environment vendors for each domain (Aria and Arcverex for chip design, Arithmetic for cyber, Latch Bio for biology, etc.). Each partner underwent QA checks for consistency, completeness, unfair graders, and other failure modes—a process that flags roughly 50% of tasks as broken in popular benchmarks like Terminal Bench 4.0.

Results show frontier models still perform poorly on the hardest domains. Even the best model scores just 12% overall. Opus 5.5 leads across hardware, quant trading, and chip design. GPT-6 Astra wins on recursive self-improvement and materials science. Gemini 4 Carbon edges out software engineering and leads on biology. Finance and legal tasks remain so challenging that most models score zero. Notably, Muse Wonder Full ranks best on cybersecurity—a reminder that safety classifiers often suppress performance in contested domains.
stories.why_it_matters: For your workshop teaching and consulting work, GDPx offers concrete visibility into where frontier models actually deliver value. It distinguishes genuine agentic progress (navigating rich, multi-file environments; applying domain expertise under uncertainty) from narrow task completion. The benchmark also surfaces how safety classifiers trade off capability for caution—critical context when advising clients on model selection for sensitive work. Understanding which domains remain hard (finance, legal) and which are settling (software engineering) helps you advise on realistic deployment timelines.
stories.potential_use: Use GDPx domain results as teaching examples in workshops—show how a finance task's difficulty comes from information retrieval and synthesis, not raw reasoning. For consulting clients in biotech, materials, or cybersecurity, reference the benchmark results to set realistic expectations about current model maturity. For your AI expertise building, the article's critique of GDPval's design flaws (rubric-based grading, vague criteria, broken links) provides a mental model for how to evaluate evaluation frameworks themselves.

sources.title: GDPx: Measuring Frontier Model Capabilities Across the Most Valuable Domains

stories.headline: Texas permit freeze threatens 2028 AI compute buildout as bipartisan backlash widens
stories.dek: Most 2027 datacenter capacity is already under construction, but regulatory delays in key states could slow the 62 GW pipeline planned for 2028.
stories.summary:
Regulatory pressure on datacenter expansion has shifted from speculation to material risk. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality froze permits in September, and Oregon expanded its earlier moratorium through July 2027. Together with tighter review processes and moratorium proposals in other states, these actions now threaten projects that have not yet broken ground.

The timing matters sharply. About three-quarters of the 33.8 GW due in 2027 is already under construction—largely insulated from new rules. But 2028 is different. Of the 62.2 GW forecast for that year, most remains in permitting or early planning stages. Thirteen states account for 70% of that capacity and hold midterm elections today. Ten of those states elect governors.

The political split is narrower than it might seem. Of the 20 major candidates, nine campaign on pausing new construction entirely while 11 want stricter conditions—requiring developers to fund grid upgrades, pay infrastructure costs, and disclose environmental data. The decisive risk is duration. If Texas keeps its freeze through the January-May 2027 legislative session, projects could lose six to nine months. Texas alone adds nearly 30% of U.S. annual datacenter capacity, so delays there ripple nationally. Larger hyperscalers like Amazon and Google can absorb higher development costs; smaller operators and vendors cannot. The constraint is not money but permitting timelines and power delivery schedules that don't compress.
stories.why_it_matters: For AI consultancy and implementation work, this directly affects what you can promise clients about compute access and timelines. A sustained permitting freeze doesn't just raise costs—it compresses available capacity in specific geographies and years, forcing enterprises to compete harder for resources or rethink where they locate inference workloads. Understanding which states will likely impose conditions versus moratoriums shapes realistic AI scaling strategy and helps identify which infrastructure partners will face execution risk.
stories.potential_use: Workshop angle: Use this as a grounded case study in "AI implementation constraints beyond the model"—showing how real-world infrastructure, regulatory, and resource scarcity affect what teams can actually deploy. Consulting angle: Help clients audit their datacenter partner's permitting exposure in 2028; ask which projects still need state approval and what conditions each state is likely to impose. India ecosystem note: Watch how Indian states begin responding to similar pressure as large AI model training and inference clusters expand; early regulatory patterns elsewhere often surface months later in India's policy forums.

sources.title: The Datacenter Backlash Goes Bipartisan: Next Week's Midterms and the 2028 Buildout
